Queue.dc.html.title: An agent is refused; you answer

s1.text:
THE SYSTEM

Instrument Sans throughout, IBM Plex Mono for the three things that are genuinely machine text: hostnames, the key, the build log. UBC Blue #003468 owns the brand mark and every primary action.

FIVE STATES AND NOTHING ELSE

Working — moving on its own, you may leave. Teal, a drifting bar, never a spinner.
Waiting on someone — a person or an office has it. Amber, and it says how long.
Needs you — stuck until you act. Red.
Steady — it works. Green.
Not yet — real, but no clock has started. Grey, hatched.

The rule: motion means a machine is moving; stillness plus a number means a person has it. So nothing measured in weeks is ever animated.

s2.text:
WHERE THE COPY COMES FROM

Real fixture values, verbatim: the slug, all three hostnames, the twenty build log lines, 135 packages, the scan counts (0 fixable, 2 unfixable High, 18 on the base image), the token secret, the 42-second wait, the incident's repair prompt.

Written for this prototype: the faculty-legible sentence for each event and each launch item. The API's own strings there — "The PIA workflow is the external track", "Custom domains are not built in Phase 1" — are internal vocabulary and would fail C3 on a faculty screen. That is finding F2.

s3.text:
All three explain their own rule on screen rather than in a help page.

A faculty member meets this platform about six times a year. They will not carry a mental model between visits, so every unusual rule — the key that cannot be shown twice, the second sign-in, the agent that must ask — re-explains itself at the moment it bites.

s4.text:
The full authoring flow, at Rich's direction, plus the conversation list.

It hands back to the real journey: "Yes, build that" goes to Provision, the same screen the hand-made route reaches.

A CONVERSATION IS THE ONE OBJECT WITH NO COUNTERPART IN THE API. Builds, releases, deploys and pending actions all exist — nothing records which piece of work they belonged to. Finding F13.

In the last artboard only the asking is invented. The refusal, the question it raises and the single retry a yes buys are built and clicked today.

s5.text:
THE PREVIEW

The app drawn inside the frame is markup, not a live embed — this format cannot carry an iframe. In the real product it would be one, and that is not free: the app is behind CWL, so an embedded preview needs a session the platform has no way to hand it, and a cross-origin frame of a SAML-protected app is blocked by default. Finding F12.

The environment switcher is honest about the fixtures: sandbox and production both have no instance, so both show an empty state rather than a mock.
